_about: Guest-safe tasting record for the Ask Jake chat: every logged wine NOT currently in the cellar, from the Notion Wine Library. No prices, buy ceilings, sources, or scoring-system notes. tried=false means Jake hasn't tasted it. onList=true means it's on his list to buy or try. verdict: 'buy again' | 'depends' | 'not for me' | null.
profile: I'm a mountain Cabernet guy. My favorite wines come from Howell Mountain, Mount Veeder and Spring Mountain in Napa: firm structure, real tannin, dark fruit with some earth underneath. My biggest test is what happens after you open it. The great ones keep getting better in the glass for hours, and if a wine goes flat, I'm out, no matter what the label says. The other way a wine wins me over is age: fully integrated and silky, but with enough backbone left for a ribeye. Restraint is great when there's real substance behind it and boring when there isn't. I don't go for sweet oak, jammy fruit-forward Cab, or wines built for the label. Lately I'm getting into Cabernet Franc-led wines like Viader and Dakota Shy. I like Right Bank Bordeaux to open a night. On weeknights I want value that overdelivers. Burgundy and Pinot are my blind spot so far.
scaleNote: Jake Score is a range out of 100, and every wine is judged against the job it's bought for. A Tuesday Night wine in the high 80s is a good bottle doing its job; it just won't blow anyone away. The top of the scale is the 2017 O'Shaughnessy Howell Mountain at 98-100.

wines.name: One & Only Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.take: Extraordinary. Earthy, fully integrated, and still had the backbone for a ribeye. A hair below my gold standard.

wines.name: Howell Mountain Cabernet
wines.take: The top wine of our August 2026 Napa trip, tasted in their cave.

wines.name: East Elevation
wines.take: Kept building for four-plus hours after decanting. One of my benchmark wines, and a producer I want to explore more.

wines.name: Viader (Proprietary Red)
wines.take: Tasted at the estate in August 2026. About 40% Cab Franc, and a big reason I'm into Cab Franc now.

wines.name: Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.take: Huge value. Stood up to a prime ribeye and kept building in the glass.

wines.name: Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.take: Classic, restrained Napa. Still sharp and young even after a two-hour decant, so it'll be better with a few more years.

wines.name: Napa Valley Cabernet
wines.take: Serious for such a young wine.

wines.name: Black Label
wines.take: Bacon and maple over an earthy backbone, softer than I expected. Strong, just short of my top tier. No smoke taint from the 2020 fires.
wines.pairing: Prime ribeye after a three-hour decant

wines.name: Mount Veeder Cabernet
wines.take: A regular in my rotation.

wines.name: Oakville Ranch Cabernet Franc
wines.take: Tasted at the winery in August 2026. One of the two Cab Francs that won me over on that trip.

wines.name: Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.take: Higher-tier Napa structure.

wines.name: Mountain Select Cabernet
wines.take: The best structure for the money I've found in mountain Cab. Built beautifully in the glass.

wines.name: Mount Veeder Cabernet
wines.take: A great-value mountain Cab that really opens up after decanting.

wines.name: Claret
wines.take: Beat the Trefethen head to head with the same steak. Structure over brand name, and strong value.

wines.name: Napa Cabernet
wines.take: Structured and right in my wheelhouse.

wines.name: Terra 9
wines.take: Polished and elegant, held all night. The 2019 is a step up.

wines.name: Les Cadrans de Lassègue
wines.take: My favorite way to open a night. Right Bank Bordeaux that goes with almost anything.

wines.name: Merlot
wines.take: The best Merlot I've had. It might change my mind about how high Merlot can go.

wines.name: 1er Vin
wines.take: Earthy and structured without overdoing the tannin. A great opener, and Fronsac is my pick with pork.

wines.name: Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.take: Safe and structured.

wines.name: St. Helena Cabernet
wines.take: Restrained Napa done right. The restraint has real substance behind it. I'd buy it on a good deal.

wines.name: Malbec
wines.take: Overdelivers for a weeknight bottle. I'd stock up.

wines.name: Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.take: Great with red-sauce pizza. The cooler-climate acidity meets the tomato where a big mountain Cab would fight it.

wines.name: Napa Valley Cabernet
wines.take: Solid Napa structure. A good everyday Cab, not a big-night wine.

wines.name: Rioja Reserva
wines.take: Great value and very comfortable with red sauce.

wines.name: Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.take: Good structure and it kept building in the glass, but softer than the mountain wines I prefer.

wines.name: Côtes de Bourg
wines.take: Merlot-led, steady all night, just doesn't build. Good with pork chops.

wines.name: Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.take: A dependable Tuesday night Cab from the Caymus family. Won't blow anyone away, but it does its job.

wines.name: Pauillac
wines.take: Grippy, real Bordeaux from Costco. A stock-up weeknight bottle.

wines.name: Allomi Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.take: A good-value pour before dinner. Front-loaded with a lighter finish, but it did its job.

wines.name: Red
wines.take: Interesting, just not really my style.

wines.name: Pinot Noir
wines.take: Perfectly fine, just not my style.

wines.name: Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.take: More fruit-forward than I like, but it worked with Thai food, where softer fruit handles the spice better than mountain tannin.

wines.name: Reserva Tinto
wines.take: Overdelivers for the price. Weeknight value.

wines.name: Valle de Guadalupe Red
wines.take: Excellent with walleye, forgettable on its own.

wines.name: Reserva
wines.take: Good with an oil-based sausage pasta, light and not much fun on its own.

wines.name: Oak Knoll Cabernet
wines.take: Restrained and hollow. Lost head to head to the Ramey Claret.

wines.name: Claret
wines.take: Didn't work with the dish, and the food did all the heavy lifting.

wines.name: Gevrey-Chambertin
wines.take: Too lean for me. It's the only Burgundy I've logged, so I don't judge the whole region on it.

wines.name: Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.take: Visited on the August 2026 trip. Too much sweet oak for my taste.

wines.name: Red
wines.take: Went flat in the glass. That's the one thing I won't forgive.

wines.name: Haut-Médoc
wines.take: First look was just okay, but it was young and poured after a much bigger wine. I'll try it again after 2028.

wines.name: Napa Valley Cabernet
wines.take: Firm mountain Cab that needed a two-to-three-hour decant. Haven't scored it yet.

wines.name: Reserva
wines.take: Liked it and would grab it again, just didn't score it.

wines.name: Sangiovese
wines.take: Good value with pork chops. I like to keep a few around.

wines.name: Riesling
wines.take: An excellent pairing with spring pea soup at a tasting dinner.

wines.name: Crémant d'Alsace
wines.take: Fantastic sparkling to start a dinner.

wines.name: Les Lavandières
wines.take: Outstanding when I had it at dinner. Didn't formally score it, but it's on my list.

wines.name: Listrac-Médoc
wines.take: Haven't tasted it. On my list as an opener.

wines.name: Monthélie Les Duresses 1er Cru
wines.take: Haven't had it yet. It's the Burgundy I most want to try.

wines.name: Jayson "The Bench"
wines.take: Still haven't tasted it. On my list.
